intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the maze-like streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from legendary local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking food tour or explore independently using a street food map.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, a beautifully preserved trading port filled with colorful lanterns, French colonial architecture, and Vietnamese temples. Visit during the monthly Lantern Festival when motorbikes are banned and the town glows with hundreds of silk lanterns. Sample Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from local market stalls.

experiences.name: Motorbiking the Hai Van Pass
experiences.description: Rent a semi-automatic motorbike and ride the legendary Hai Van Pass, a dramatic mountain road stretching between Da Nang and Hue offering breathtaking coastal views, jungle scenery, and an authentic backpacker rite of passage in Vietnam. Stop at the old French and American war bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of the South China Sea.
experiences.location: Hai Van Pass, between Da Nang and Hue

experiences.name: Mekong Delta Boat Tour & Local Village Visit
experiences.description: Take a budget day trip from Ho Chi Minh City into the Mekong Delta, cruising narrow waterways by wooden sampan boat through floating markets, rice paddies, and coconut groves. Visit local workshops producing rice paper, coconut candy, and honey, and share a home-cooked lunch with a Vietnamese family in a riverside village.

experiences.name: Bui Vien Walking Street Night Experience
experiences.description: Dive into the heart of Ho Chi Minh City's legendary backpacker district on Bui Vien Street. Grab a plastic stool on the sidewalk, order a Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer for under $1), and feast on grilled skewers, Banh Trang Nuong (Vietnamese pizza), and fresh spring rolls from street carts while soaking in the electric atmosphere of live music and fellow travelers from around the world.
experiences.location: Bui Vien Street, Pham Ngu Lao Backpacker District, Ho Chi Minh City

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly airport bus (86 Express, ~45 min, ~45,000 VND) to the Old Quarter. Check in to Old Quarter Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around Hoan Kiem Lake (10-min walk from most Old Quarter hostels). Admire the Turtle Tower and Ngoc Son Temple from the lakeside promenade - free to walk around.
day_by_day.evening: Dive straight into the Old Quarter's famous '36 Streets' night buzz. Explore the pedestrian weekend market streets (Hang Dao area). Grab a plastic stool on Ta Hien Street ('Beer Street') for a 10,000 VND Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer) and soak in the backpacker atmosphere. Early night recommended to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab Banh Mi from a street cart near the Old Quarter upon arrival (~25,000-35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Cha at a local Old Quarter stall on Hang Manh or Ly Quoc Su Street (~50,000-70,000 VND). Follow with Bia Hoi on Ta Hien Street (~10,000-15,000 VND per glass)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to VND at the airport (rates are decent) or use a local ATM. Avoid taxi touts - use the 86 Express bus or book a Grab (Vietnamese Uber) for ~250,000 VND. Keep your bag close in the busy Old Quarter streets.

day_by_day.morning: Start early with a bowl of Pho at a famous local spot on Bat Dan Street (Pho Bat Dan opens at 6am, ~50,000 VND). Walk to Hoan Kiem Lake for the morning tai chi scene with locals - a beautiful and completely free cultural experience. Cross the red Huc Bridge to visit Ngoc Son Temple (~30,000 VND entrance). Browse the surrounding streets as the city wakes up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (free, closed Mondays & Fridays and 11:30am-2pm). Visit the surrounding Ba Dinh Square, the Presidential Palace gardens, and Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House (~40,000 VND). Walk to the nearby One Pillar Pagoda (free). Then explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology if interested in deeper culture (~40,000 VND, take a Grab ~25,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Quarter for the famous Hanoi Street Food Tour on foot. Visit Hang Be Market area. Try Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) on Thanh Nien, then Nem Ran (fried spring rolls). End the evening with Egg Coffee (Ca Phe Trung) at the iconic Cafe Giang on Nguyen Huu Huan Street (~30,000 VND) - a Hanoi must-do.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bat Dan on Bat Dan Street (~50,000 VND) - arrive before 7am for the best experience
meals.lunch: Bun Rieu (crab noodle soup) from a street vendor near the mausoleum area (~40,000-50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Street food crawl: Banh Cuon (~30,000 VND) + Nem Ran (~20,000 VND) + Egg Coffee at Cafe Giang (~30,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum - no shorts or sleeveless tops. The mausoleum requires you to walk in silence and keep moving. Total day budget including transport: ~250,000-300,000 VND (~$10-12 USD).

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17, 2027 (Hanoi Deep Dive & Hoa Lo Prison)
day_by_day.morning: Visit Hoa Lo Prison Museum ('Hanoi Hilton') - a powerful and sobering cultural site (~30,000 VND, 10-min walk from Old Quarter). Spend 1.5-2 hours exploring. Afterward, walk to St. Joseph's Cathedral (free, check mass times) in the French Quarter - beautiful colonial architecture perfect for photos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the French Quarter on foot - admire the colonial architecture along Trang Tien and Ngo Quyen streets. Visit the Vietnam Fine Arts Museum (~30,000 VND) for a look at traditional and contemporary Vietnamese art. Alternatively, browse the Dong Xuan Market (free entry) - Hanoi's largest covered market - for cheap souvenirs, local goods, and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Thang Long Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Theatre on Dinh Tien Hoang Street (~100,000 VND for standard seats - book same day at the box office). This 1,000-year-old art form is a bucket-list Vietnam experience. Afterward, grab dinner at a nearby Old Quarter restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street cart near the hotel (~20,000-30,000 VND) - a classic Hanoi breakfast
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan (everyday rice with dishes) at a local canteen near Dong Xuan Market (~40,000-60,000 VND for a full plate)
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong (turmeric fish with dill) - the iconic Hanoi dish - at a budget version on Cha Ca Street (~120,000-150,000 VND, splurge-worthy)

day_by_day.notes: The Water Puppet Show runs multiple times daily (usually 3pm, 5pm, 6:30pm, 8pm). The 6:30pm show is ideal after sightseeing. Book tickets at the box office 30-60 min before. Total day budget: ~350,000-400,000 VND (~$14-16 USD).

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18, 2027 (Day Trip to Ninh Binh)
day_by_day.morning: Take an early bus from Giap Bat Bus Station or My Dinh Bus Station to Ninh Binh (~2 hours, ~80,000-100,000 VND each way - book via Grab or walk-in). Arrive by 9am. Rent a bicycle near Ninh Binh town (~50,000-80,000 VND/day) or hire a local xe om (motorbike taxi). Head to Trang An Landscape Complex - take a 2-hour boat tour through stunning limestone karsts and caves (~250,000 VND, includes boat and rower).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or take transport to Bich Dong Pagoda (free, ~15,000 VND parking) - a beautiful pagoda built into a limestone cliff with cave temples. Climb to the upper pagoda for panoramic views. Then visit Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (~20,000 VND) - Vietnam's 10th-century capital with historic temples. Cycle through the scenic countryside between sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ninh Binh town for a quick dinner before catching the evening bus back to Hanoi (last buses around 6-7pm). Back in the Old Quarter by 9pm. Rest up for the overnight train tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Quick Banh Mi or Xoi near the bus station before departure (~20,000-30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Chay (Ninh Binh's famous goat meat rice or vegetarian version) at a local restaurant in Ninh Binh town (~60,000-80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: De Nuong (grilled goat) - Ninh Binh's specialty - at a local eatery before the bus back (~80,000-100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Ninh Binh is one of Vietnam's most stunning landscapes and easily doable as a day trip. Alternatively, book a budget guesthouse in Ninh Binh (~150,000-200,000 VND/night) and spend two days. Total day trip budget: ~600,000-700,000 VND (~$24-28 USD) including transport.

day_by_day.date: Day 5 - April 19, 2027 (Travel to Hue via Overnight Train)
day_by_day.morning: Last morning in Hanoi. Pack your bag and store luggage at the hotel if needed. Take a final walk around Hoan Kiem Lake. Visit the Dong Xuan Market for any last-minute cheap souvenir shopping (lacquerware, silk scarves, conical hats). Try any Hanoi street food you missed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel. Spend the afternoon at a budget cafe with WiFi to plan ahead (Cong Caphe on Trieu Viet Vuong is popular, ~35,000-45,000 VND for drinks). Head to Hanoi Railway Station (Ga Ha Noi) on Le Duan Street - about a 15-min walk or short Grab from the Old Quarter. Your train departs in the evening (book SE3 or SE7 train, ~300,000-400,000 VND for a 6-berth sleeper).
day_by_day.evening: Board the overnight train to Hue (~14 hours). Get settled in your sleeper berth. Chat with fellow backpackers and travelers. The train journey itself is a classic Vietnam backpacker experience with scenic views at dawn.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Banh Mi from a nearby Old Quarter stall for a final Hanoi breakfast (~40,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Com Binh Dan lunch near Hoan Kiem Lake (~50,000-60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Buy snacks and instant noodles from shops near the train station (~30,000-50,000 VND). Train vendors also sell basic food onboard (~30,000-50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets in advance at baolau.com, 12go.asia, or directly at the station. The SE3 train (departs ~19:00) or SE7 (departs ~22:00) are good options. A 6-berth hard sleeper is the budget choice (~300,000-350,000 VND). Bring earplugs and a travel pillow. Total day budget: ~500,000-600,000 VND (~$20-24 USD).

day_by_day.morning: Arrive in Hue by morning (~9-10am). Check into a budget guesthouse or hostel in the city center (~150,000-200,000 VND/night). Freshen up and head to the Imperial Citadel (Dai Noi) - the UNESCO-listed walled city of the Nguyen Dynasty (~200,000 VND entrance). Spend 2-3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City, the Thai Hoa Palace, and the beautifully restored halls. Rent a bicycle to get around (~50,000-80,000 VND/day).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to the Royal Tombs south of Hue along the Perfume River. Visit Tu Duc Tomb (~100,000 VND) - the most romantic and picturesque of the royal tombs, set in a forested landscape with lakes and pavilions. Alternatively, visit Minh Mang Tomb (~100,000 VND) for its grand Confucian symmetry. The cycling route along the river is scenic and free.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Dong Ba Market area on the north bank of the Perfume River. Watch the sunset from Truong Tien Bridge. Explore Hue's vibrant evening food scene on the south bank around Pham Ngu Lao Street.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or instant noodles on the train, or grab Bun Bo Hue (Hue's famous spicy beef noodle soup) immediately upon arrival (~50,000-60,000 VND) - this is the best city to try it
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) at a local eatery near Dong Ba Market (~30,000-40,000 VND) - a Hue specialty
meals.dinner: Banh Khoai (Hue sizzling pancake) and Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes) at a local restaurant on Vo Thi Sau Street (~60,000-80,000 VND for a spread of dishes)

day_by_day.notes: Hue is known for its royal cuisine - many dishes are small and meant to be shared. Try as many local specialties as possible. The Imperial Citadel is large - wear comfortable shoes. Total day budget: ~600,000-700,000 VND (~$24-28 USD).

day_by_day.date: Day 7 - April 21, 2027 (Hue to Hoi An via Hai Van Pass)
day_by_day.morning: Take a motorbike or join a budget group tour over the legendary Hai Van Pass to Hoi An (~150,000-200,000 VND by local bus or ~300,000-400,000 VND for a shared motorbike tour). The Hai Van Pass ('Pass of Ocean Clouds') offers some of the most dramatic coastal scenery in Southeast Asia. Stop at the old French/American bunkers at the summit for panoramic views of Da Nang Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An Ancient Town (~3-4 hours from Hue). Check into a budget guesthouse in or near the Ancient Town (~150,000-250,000 VND/night). Buy a combined Ancient Town ticket (~120,000 VND - required to enter most heritage sites). Visit 3-4 sites included in the ticket: Tan Ky Old House, the Japanese Covered Bridge, the Assembly Halls, and a traditional craft workshop.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the Ancient Town at dusk as the famous lanterns illuminate the streets - one of Vietnam's most magical sights. Walk along the Thu Bon River. Browse the lantern and handicraft shops. The Ancient Town is pedestrian-only in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Bun Bo Hue or Banh Mi before departure from Hue (~40,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~60,000-80,000 VND) - this dish is unique to Hoi An
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Banh Mi Phuong (Hoi An's famous banh mi, featured by Anthony Bourdain) on Phan Chau Trinh Street (~20,000-30,000 VND per banh mi)

day_by_day.notes: The bus from Hue to Hoi An via Da Nang costs ~100,000-150,000 VND (3.5-4 hours) and is the cheapest option. For the iconic Hai Van Pass experience, hire a motorbike driver in Hue (~300,000-400,000 VND) - worth every dong. Total travel day budget: ~500,000-600,000 VND (~$20-24 USD).

day_by_day.date: Day 8 - April 22, 2027 (Hoi An - Beaches & Cooking Class)
day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000-80,000 VND/day) and cycle 5km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach - Hoi An's beautiful, relatively uncrowded beaches. Swim and relax in the morning before the heat peaks. The cycle through rice paddies and villages is scenic and peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town. Join a budget cooking class (~300,000-500,000 VND) - Hoi An is one of the best places in Vietnam to learn Vietnamese cooking. Classes typically include a market tour, hands-on cooking of 3-4 dishes, and eating your creations. Alternatively, visit the Hoi An Museum of History and Culture (~30,000 VND) and explore the craft villages (Thanh Ha Pottery Village, ~35,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Hoi An Night Market on An Hoi Island (cross the footbridge from the Ancient Town). Browse handmade lanterns, clothing, and street food. Watch locals release paper lanterns on the Thu Bon River (~10,000-20,000 VND per lantern). This is one of Vietnam's most photogenic evening experiences.

meals.breakfast: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with pork/shrimp) at a local eatery near the market (~40,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Eat at the beach - fresh coconut (~20,000 VND) and a simple rice dish from a beach shack (~60,000-80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Night market street food: Com Ga (Hoi An chicken rice, ~50,000 VND) + fresh spring rolls + grilled corn (~10,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is famous for cheap custom tailoring - if interested, get measured on Day 7 or early Day 8 for a 24-48 hour turnaround. A simple dress or shirt costs ~200,000-400,000 VND. The full moon lantern festival (15th of each lunar month) is spectacular if timing aligns. Total day budget: ~400,000-600,000 VND (~$16-24 USD).

day_by_day.date: Day 9 - April 23, 2027 (Travel to Ho Chi Minh City - Saigon)
day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hoi An. Visit the colorful Hoi An Central Market for a last browse and breakfast. Pick up any tailored clothing ordered earlier. Check out of guesthouse. Take a Grab or local bus to Da Nang Airport (~30km, ~150,000-200,000 VND by Grab). Fly to Ho Chi Minh City (book in advance with VietJet or Bamboo Airways, ~400,000-800,000 VND one-way).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Take bus 109 from Tan Son Nhat Airport to the city center (~20,000 VND) or a Grab (~100,000-150,000 VND). Check into a budget hostel in District 1 or the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker area (~120,000-200,000 VND/night). Drop bags and head out to explore the Pham Ngu Lao backpacker district.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ben Thanh Market area (closes around 6pm for the indoor market, but the surrounding street stalls continue). Walk to the iconic Saigon Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Central Post Office (free, beautiful French colonial architecture). Watch the crazy Saigon traffic from a street-side cafe. Join the evening buzz on Bui Vien Walking Street.

meals.breakfast: Final Cao Lau or Banh Mi Phuong in Hoi An before departure (~30,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport snack or eat after arriving in HCMC - grab Banh Mi from a cart near the hostel (~25,000-35,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bun Thit Nuong (grilled pork vermicelli) or Hu Tieu (southern noodle soup) at a local pho stall in District 1 (~50,000-70,000 VND). Follow with a fresh fruit smoothie from a street cart (~20,000-30,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang to HCMC flight well in advance for the best prices (~400,000-600,000 VND). Alternatively, take an overnight sleeper bus (~200,000-300,000 VND, ~18 hours) to save on accommodation costs. HCMC is significantly hotter and more chaotic than Hanoi - be prepared. Total travel day budget: ~800,000-1,000,000 VND (~$32-40 USD including flight).

day_by_day.date: Day 10 - April 24, 2027 (Ho Chi Minh City - Final Day)
day_by_day.morning: Start with a visit to the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) - one of Vietnam's most important and moving museums documenting the Vietnam War. Allow 2 hours. Walk to the Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) - the former South Vietnamese presidential palace, frozen in time since 1975, with its famous war-era command bunkers underground.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore District 1's street life. Visit Nguyen Hue Walking Street and the Ho Chi Minh City Hall (exterior, free). Head to the Ben Thanh Market area for souvenir shopping - bargain hard (start at 50% of asking price). Visit a local Saigon cafe - try Ca Phe Sua Da (Vietnamese iced coffee with condensed milk, ~20,000-30,000 VND) at a local spot, not a tourist cafe. Alternatively, take a half-day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~150,000-200,000 VND entrance + ~100,000-150,000 VND transport) if time allows.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Vietnam. Head to a rooftop bar in District 1 for a sundowner with city views (Saigon Saigon Bar at Caravelle Hotel has happy hour prices). Enjoy a final Vietnamese street food feast on De Tham or Bui Vien Street. Reflect on the incredible 10-day journey through Vietnam's north, centre, and south.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Op La (baguette with fried eggs) from a street cart near the hostel (~25,000-35,000 VND) - a classic Saigon breakfast
meals.lunch: Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork, egg, and pickled vegetables) at a local Com Tam restaurant (~50,000-70,000 VND) - the quintessential Saigon dish
meals.dinner: Lau (Vietnamese hot pot) at a budget local restaurant on Bui Vien Street shared with fellow backpackers (~100,000-150,000 VND per person) for a festive final meal. End with Che (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup, ~20,000-30,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: If flying home late tonight or early tomorrow, store bags at the hostel and enjoy the full day. Grab to the airport costs ~150,000-200,000 VND (allow 45-60 min in traffic). Total final day budget: ~400,000-500,000 VND (~$16-20 USD). Overall 10-day trip budget estimate: ~6,000,000-8,000,000 VND (~$240-320 USD) excluding international flights, including accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hanoi Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Old Quarter boutique hotel (~45 min by taxi or Grab app, ~200,000–300,000 VND). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a relaxed self-guided walk through the 36 Streets of the Old Quarter. Explore Hang Gai (Silk Street), Hang Bac (Silver Street), and the vibrant alleyways. Stop at Hoan Kiem Lake to see Ngoc Son Temple from the red Huc Bridge (entry ~30,000 VND). Great way to ease into the city's energy.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ta Hien Street ('Beer Street') for a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, ~5,000–10,000 VND per glass) and soak up the buzzing Old Quarter nightlife. Browse the Hanoi Night Market on Hang Dao Street (open Fri–Sun evenings) for local crafts and street snacks.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a light snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Bun Cha Huong Lien (Obama's famous spot) — grilled pork with noodles ~60,000–80,000 VND, a short walk from the Old Quarter.
meals.dinner: Pho Thin on Lo Duc Street or a local pho stall near the hotel — a classic bowl of Hanoi-style beef pho (~50,000–70,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab app for affordable and reliable transport from the airport. Exchange some cash to VND at the airport or an ATM in the Old Quarter. April weather in Hanoi is warm (~28°C) with occasional drizzle — pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex (open Tue–Thu & Sat–Sun mornings, closed Mon & Fri; free entry but check schedule). See the Presidential Palace gardens, Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Dress modestly and arrive early (~8:00 AM) to avoid queues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology (~40,000 VND entry) — one of Southeast Asia's best cultural museums showcasing 54 ethnic groups. Spend 2–3 hours here. Afterward, cycle or take a Grab to the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu), Vietnam's first university (~30,000 VND entry).
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Water Puppet Show at Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre near Hoan Kiem Lake (~100,000 VND). Book tickets in advance. Stroll the lakeside promenade after the show.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi from a street cart near the hotel — a fresh baguette sandwich with pate, cold cuts, and pickled veggies (~25,000–40,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Bun Cha at a local restaurant near the Museum of Ethnology (~60,000 VND) or Bun Bo Nam Bo (dry beef noodles) at a nearby stall.
meals.dinner: Cha Ca La Vong on Cha Ca Street — Hanoi's iconic turmeric fish dish cooked tableside with dill (~150,000–200,000 VND per person, mid-range splurge).

day_by_day.notes: The Mausoleum is closed on Mondays and Fridays — confirm the day before. Wear covered shoulders and knees for temple visits. Bargain politely at souvenir stalls.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Ninh Binh (2 hours by bus from My Dinh or Giap Bat bus station, ~100,000 VND). Rent a bicycle (~50,000 VND/day) upon arrival and cycle to Tam Coc — the 'Halong Bay on land.' Take a 2-hour rowing boat trip through limestone karsts and rice paddies (~150,000 VND).
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle to Bich Dong Pagoda (free entry), a stunning cave pagoda carved into the hillside. Climb to the upper cave for panoramic views of the valley. Optionally visit Hoa Lu Ancient Capital (~20,000 VND), the 10th-century dynastic seat with ornate temples.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Hanoi by bus or shared minivan. Rest at the hotel, then explore the Old Quarter night market or grab a quiet dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a street vendor near the hotel — filling and cheap (~20,000–30,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Rang (fried rice) or Bun Cha at a local eatery in Ninh Binh town (~60,000 VND) — ask locals for recommendations.
meals.dinner: Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) at a small restaurant in the Old Quarter (~50,000–70,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Book Ninh Binh bus tickets the evening before from the hotel or online. Start early (7:00–7:30 AM bus) to maximize time there. Bring sunscreen and water — cycling in April heat can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Take an overnight sleeper bus or early morning train to Hue (depart ~6:00–7:00 AM, ~12–14 hours by train or 11 hours by bus). Book a mid-range sleeper bus (~200,000–300,000 VND) for comfort. Enjoy the scenic coastal route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Traveling en route. The train/bus passes through beautiful mountain passes and coastal scenery — keep your camera ready for the Hai Van Pass views if taking the train.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Hue in the evening (~7:00–8:00 PM). Check into a guesthouse or boutique hostel in the city center (~200,000–400,000 VND/night). Stroll along the Perfume River and explore Dong Ba Market area for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pho or Bun Cha at a nearby Old Quarter stall before departure (~50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or buy food at train/bus stops — instant noodles, boiled eggs, and fresh fruit are commonly sold (~30,000–50,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Bun Bo Hue (spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup) at a local restaurant near your guesthouse — a must-try Hue specialty (~50,000–70,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Book train tickets (SE trains) or sleeper bus at least 2–3 days in advance, especially around Vietnamese holidays. The Reunification Express train is scenic but slower — budget travelers often prefer the sleeper bus for cost savings.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Imperial Citadel of Hue (Dai Noi) — the massive 19th-century Nguyen Dynasty fortress (~150,000 VND entry). Spend 2–3 hours exploring the Forbidden Purple City ruins, ceremonial gates, and royal gardens. Hire a local guide (~100,000–150,000 VND) for historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike (~100,000–150,000 VND/day) and ride along the Perfume River to visit the Royal Tombs. Recommended: Tu Duc Tomb (~100,000 VND) and Minh Mang Tomb (~100,000 VND) — both architecturally stunning and set in forested grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Thien Mu Pagoda (free) at sunset for beautiful river views. Return to the city and explore the Hue Night Market near Dong Ba Bridge for local crafts, street food, and Vietnamese snacks.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Mi Quang (turmeric noodles) at a local street stall (~30,000–50,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Hen (baby clam rice) or Banh Khoai (Hue-style crispy pancake) at Lac Thien Restaurant — a famous deaf-family-run local institution (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Banh Beo (steamed rice cakes with shrimp) and Nem Lui (lemongrass skewers) at a local Hue restaurant (~80,000–120,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Hue's royal cuisine is one of Vietnam's most refined — try as many local specialties as possible. The city is compact and very bikeable. April is warm (~30°C) — stay hydrated during outdoor visits.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus or open-tour bus to Hoi An (~3.5–4 hours, ~100,000–150,000 VND). Alternatively, hire a motorbike driver to cross the scenic Hai Van Pass (~300,000–400,000 VND for the experience). Arrive in Hoi An by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a guesthouse in or near Hoi An Ancient Town (~250,000–450,000 VND/night). Explore the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town on foot — visit the Japanese Covered Bridge, Tan Ky Old House (~80,000 VND), Chinese Assembly Halls, and colorful lantern-lit streets.
day_by_day.evening: Join a lantern-lit evening walk through the Ancient Town. Buy a paper lantern (~20,000–30,000 VND) and release it on the Thu Bon River for good luck. Explore the lively riverside restaurants and bars.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the bus or grab a quick Banh Mi before departure.
meals.lunch: Cao Lau (Hoi An's signature thick noodle dish with pork and greens) at Thanh Cao Lau or a local stall — only authentic in Hoi An (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: White Rose Dumplings (Banh Bao Vac) and Hoanh Thanh (wontons) at a riverside restaurant in the Ancient Town (~100,000–150,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: The Ancient Town charges a ticket for entry to heritage sites (combined ticket ~120,000 VND for 5 sites). Hoi An is famous for custom tailoring — if interested, visit a tailor on this day for measurements so clothes are ready before you leave.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~50,000–80,000 VND/day) and cycle 5 km to An Bang Beach or Cua Dai Beach for a relaxing morning swim. April weather is ideal — warm and sunny with calm seas. Enjoy the laid-back beach vibe.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to town and take a Vietnamese cooking class (~300,000–500,000 VND) — most include a market tour, hands-on cooking of 3–4 dishes, and eating your creations. Highly recommended for food lovers.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Hoi An Night Market on Nguyen Hoang Street. Try street snacks, browse handmade crafts, and watch local performers. End the night with a drink at a rooftop bar overlooking the lantern-lit river.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — Hoi An's most famous banh mi stall, featured by Anthony Bourdain (~30,000–40,000 VND). Arrive early as lines form quickly.
meals.lunch: Eat the dishes you cook in your cooking class — a fun and delicious midday meal included in the class fee.
meals.dinner: Mi Quang (turmeric noodles with shrimp and herbs) at a local restaurant in the Ancient Town (~60,000–80,000 VND), followed by Che dessert (sweet soup) from a street cart (~20,000 VND).

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class in advance — Morning Glory Cooking School and Red Bridge Cooking School are highly rated. Hoi An is very walkable and bikeable; tuk-tuks and Grab are available for longer distances.

day_by_day.morning: Take a flight or overnight bus to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon). Morning flights from Da Nang Airport (30 min from Hoi An by Grab, ~100,000 VND) to HCMC take ~1.5 hours (~800,000–1,500,000 VND on budget airlines like VietJet or Bamboo). Arrive by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into a guesthouse or boutique hotel in District 1 or the Bui Vien backpacker area (~250,000–500,000 VND/night). Visit the War Remnants Museum (~40,000 VND) — a powerful and sobering exhibition on the Vietnam War. Then walk to Reunification Palace (~40,000 VND) nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Bui Vien Walking Street — HCMC's famous backpacker strip with neon lights, rooftop bars, and street food. Try a Saigon-style iced coffee at a sidewalk cafe and soak up the city's electric energy.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Hoi An hotel before checkout or grab airport food.
meals.lunch: Banh Mi at a local stall near your HCMC hotel (~30,000–40,000 VND) or Com Tam (broken rice with grilled pork) — a Saigon staple (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Pho Hoa Pasteur — one of HCMC's most famous pho restaurants, open since 1960 (~80,000–100,000 VND). Follow with fresh fruit from a street cart.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang–HCMC flight at least 3–4 days in advance for best prices. Use Grab from the airport to the city center (~150,000–200,000 VND, much cheaper than taxis). HCMC traffic is intense — be cautious crossing streets.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels (~40 km northwest of HCMC). Join a half-day group tour (~200,000–350,000 VND including transport and entry) or take a local bus. Explore the 250 km underground tunnel network used by Viet Cong guerrillas — a fascinating and humbling historical experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to HCMC by early afternoon. Visit Ben Thanh Market — HCMC's iconic covered market for souvenirs, clothing, and street food (bargain hard; prices start 2–3x higher). Walk to the nearby Notre-Dame Cathedral (exterior view, under renovation) and the Central Post Office — a stunning French colonial building.
day_by_day.evening: Explore District 4 or District 6 for authentic local street food away from tourist areas. Alternatively, visit a rooftop bar in District 1 (Chill Sky Bar or EON51) for sunset cocktails with panoramic city views (~150,000–250,000 VND per drink).

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi or Xoi from a street cart near the hotel (~25,000–40,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Eat at the Cu Chi Tunnels site restaurant or pack snacks — local set meals available for ~80,000–100,000 VND.
meals.dinner: Quan An Ngon on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia — a famous open-air restaurant serving dishes from all regions of Vietnam in a beautiful colonial courtyard (~100,000–200,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, dark-colored clothing to Cu Chi Tunnels (the tunnels are tight and muddy). Bring insect repellent. Book the tour through your guesthouse or a reputable agency to avoid scams.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu) in District 3 — one of HCMC's most atmospheric and ornate Taoist temples (free entry, donations welcome). Then explore the French Quarter architecture along Dong Khoi Street and Nguyen Hue Walking Boulevard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final souvenir shopping at Ben Thanh Market or the nearby Saigon Square. Visit the Fine Arts Museum (~30,000 VND) in a stunning French-Vietnamese colonial building for a cultural finale. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in HCMC. Head to the airport via Grab in advance of your flight (allow 1.5–2 hours for traffic). Tan Son Nhat Airport is about 30–45 min from District 1 (~100,000–150,000 VND by Grab).

meals.breakfast: Hu Tieu (southern-style clear noodle soup) at a local street stall — a quintessential Saigon breakfast (~50,000–70,000 VND).
meals.lunch: Com Tam Thuan Kieu or any local Com Tam stall — broken rice with grilled pork chop, fried egg, and pickled vegetables (~60,000–80,000 VND).
meals.dinner: Farewell splurge at a mid-range Vietnamese restaurant — try Nha Hang Ngon or a seafood spot in District 4 for a memorable last meal (~200,000–300,000 VND per person).

day_by_day.notes: Keep some VND for last-minute purchases and airport snacks. Vietnam has a 45-day e-visa for most nationalities — ensure your passport is valid 6 months beyond your travel dates. This 10-day trip covers Hanoi, Ninh Binh, Hue, Hoi An, and HCMC — a classic North-to-South Vietnam backpacker route balancing culture, history, nature, and incredible street food.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Noi Bai International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to Boutique Stay in the Old Quarter (approx. 45 minutes). Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the 36 Streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter. Explore the narrow lanes of Hang Gai (Silk Street) and Hang Bac (Silver Street). Visit Hoan Kiem Lake and the iconic red Huc Bridge leading to Ngoc Son Temple. Enjoy the serene lakeside atmosphere and photograph the Turtle Tower.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a world-renowned Water Puppet Show at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre (book premium front-row seats in advance). Afterward, stroll through the atmospheric Old Quarter night scene with its lantern-lit alleys and buzzing street vendors.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or at airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at the hotel or nearby Cafe Pho Co — a hidden rooftop cafe overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake, famous for its egg coffee and Vietnamese spring rolls
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Badiane — a celebrated fine-dining French-Vietnamese fusion restaurant in the French Quarter, known for its elegant tasting menus and curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light due to potential jet lag. Request a late check-out option for the next morning if needed. Ensure Water Puppet Theatre tickets are pre-booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Begin with a premium Vietnamese breakfast at the hotel, then embark on a private guided cultural tour of the Temple of Literature (Van Mieu) — Vietnam's first national university dating to 1070. Explore its five serene courtyards, ancient stone steles, and lotus ponds with an expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology — one of Southeast Asia's finest cultural museums — to discover the rich diversity of Vietnam's 54 ethnic groups through immersive exhibits and outdoor traditional house reconstructions. Afterward, explore the elegant French Quarter architecture with a private cyclo (rickshaw) tour.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the legendary Bia Hoi Corner (Ta Hien Street) for an authentic street culture experience — sip locally brewed fresh beer on tiny plastic stools alongside locals. Then transition to a premium cocktail bar experience at Polite Pub or Summit Lounge for panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Premium Vietnamese breakfast at the hotel — pho bo (beef noodle soup), banh mi, and fresh tropical fruit platter with Vietnamese drip coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cha Ca La Vong — Hanoi's most iconic restaurant serving its singular dish: cha ca (turmeric-marinated grilled fish with dill and shrimp paste), a 150-year-old culinary institution
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chim Sao — a sophisticated restaurant specializing in authentic Northern Vietnamese cuisine with rustic-chic decor and regional delicacies like sticky rice with mountain herbs

day_by_day.notes: Hire a private English-speaking guide for the Temple of Literature and Ethnology Museum for a richer experience. Dress modestly for temple visits. The French Quarter cyclo tour is best done in the late afternoon golden light.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning street food walking tour of the Old Quarter with a premium culinary guide. Sample Hanoi's iconic breakfast dishes: bun oc (snail noodle soup), banh cuon (steamed rice rolls), xoi xeo (sticky rice with mung bean), and the legendary egg coffee (ca phe trung) at Cafe Giang — the original inventor since 1946.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private visit to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex (check opening hours — closed Mondays and Fridays). Explore the Presidential Palace gardens, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house, and the One Pillar Pagoda. Continue to the Vietnam Military History Museum for fascinating wartime context.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live traditional Vietnamese music performance featuring ca tru (ceremonial singing) or quan ho folk music at a heritage venue in the Old Quarter. End the evening with a premium spa treatment at your hotel or a nearby luxury wellness center.

meals.breakfast: Street food tour breakfast — multiple tastings across 5–6 Old Quarter vendors included in the tour
meals.lunch: Lunch at Bun Cha Huong Lien — the legendary restaurant where Anthony Bourdain and President Obama famously dined together in 2016, serving Hanoi-style bun cha (grilled pork with noodles)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Maison Van Phuc — an exquisite fine-dining experience set within a restored 1930s French villa, offering contemporary Vietnamese cuisine with premium wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum requires modest dress (covered shoulders and knees). Photography is strictly prohibited inside the mausoleum. Book the culinary walking tour with Hanoi Street Food Tours or a similar premium operator for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to Ha Long Bay — depart Hanoi by private luxury transfer (approximately 3.5 hours). Board a premium overnight junk cruise (Heritage Line or Indochine Cruise recommended). Morning activities include kayaking through hidden lagoons and exploring Surprise Cave (Hang Sung Sot) — one of the bay's most spectacular grottos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cruise through the UNESCO World Heritage limestone karst landscape. Enjoy a cooking class on deck learning to prepare Vietnamese spring rolls and fresh seafood dishes. Optional Tai Chi session on the sundeck as the sun dips over the karsts.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the upper deck with panoramic views of Ha Long Bay's silhouetted limestone towers. Multi-course premium seafood dinner aboard the cruise featuring freshly caught squid, prawns, and local fish prepared by the ship's chef.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at hotel before departure or en-route stop
meals.lunch: Welcome lunch aboard the cruise — Vietnamese seafood feast with fresh spring rolls, steamed clams, and grilled fish
meals.dinner: Premium multi-course dinner aboard the junk cruise — fresh Ha Long Bay seafood including lobster, crab, and local fish with Vietnamese herbs and dipping sauces, paired with selected wines

day_by_day.notes: This is an overnight cruise — pack an overnight bag. Book the Heritage Line Jasmine or similar 5-star vessel well in advance as they sell out months ahead. The cruise includes all meals, activities, and transfers. Bring sunscreen, a light jacket for evening, and motion sickness tablets if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning sunrise on the cruise deck with panoramic karst views. Optional morning kayak or bamboo boat ride through a secluded lagoon. Visit a floating fishing village to learn about traditional Ha Long Bay fishing culture from local families.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return cruise to harbor (check-out by noon). Private luxury transfer back to Hanoi (3.5 hours) or directly to the airport for an internal flight to Hoi An via Da Nang. Check into a luxury resort in Hoi An's Ancient Town area (La Siesta Resort or Anantara Hoi An recommended).
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Hoi An — explore the magical UNESCO-listed Ancient Town at dusk as hundreds of silk lanterns illuminate the Thu Bon River. Join a lantern-making workshop at a local artisan studio, then release a paper lantern onto the river for good luck.

meals.breakfast: Full Vietnamese and Western breakfast buffet aboard the cruise
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard the cruise before disembarkation — fresh Vietnamese noodles and local specialties
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Field Restaurant, Hoi An — a stunning open-air restaurant set among rice paddies, serving refined Central Vietnamese cuisine with farm-to-table ingredients

day_by_day.notes: Internal flight from Hanoi to Da Nang (1 hour) is highly recommended over the long road transfer. Pre-book the flight as part of the trip package. Hoi An's Ancient Town is pedestrian-only in the evenings — embrace the romantic, lantern-lit atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Hoi An Ancient Town's most significant heritage sites: the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge (Lai Vien Kieu), Tan Ky Old House (a 200-year-old merchant home), Phuc Kien Assembly Hall, and the vibrant Central Market. Learn about the town's unique fusion of Japanese, Chinese, and Vietnamese trading history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium half-day cooking class at Red Bridge Cooking School — set on the Thu Bon River, accessible by boat. Learn to prepare Hoi An's signature dishes: cao lau (thick noodles with pork), white rose dumplings (banh bao vac), and crispy pancakes (banh xeo). Tour the organic herb garden.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset river cruise along the Thu Bon River on a traditional wooden boat with complimentary wine and canapes. Disembark at the Ancient Town for an evening of exploring boutique silk shops, artisan galleries, and the atmospheric lantern-lit streets.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — Vietnamese pho, fresh baguettes, tropical fruit, and ca phe sua da (Vietnamese iced coffee)
meals.lunch: Lunch prepared and enjoyed during the Red Bridge Cooking Class experience
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cargo Club Restaurant — a Hoi An institution with a rooftop terrace overlooking the river, offering refined Vietnamese and international cuisine with an excellent cocktail menu

day_by_day.notes: Purchase an Ancient Town entrance ticket (covers 5 heritage sites) from the official ticket office. Tailor-made ao dai (traditional Vietnamese dress) fittings can be arranged at Yaly Couture — order on Day 6 for pickup on Day 8. Hoi An is famous for its bespoke tailoring.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to My Son Sanctuary — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the most significant collection of Cham Hindu temples in Vietnam, dating from the 4th to 14th centuries. Explore the jungle-surrounded temple clusters with a specialist archaeological guide who brings the ancient Champa Kingdom to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An. Visit the Tra Que Vegetable Village — a picturesque organic farming community on the outskirts of town. Participate in a premium farm-to-table experience: plant vegetables, learn traditional farming techniques, and prepare a fresh village lunch using ingredients you've just harvested.
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a luxury spa evening at your resort's wellness center — traditional Vietnamese herbal steam bath, full-body massage with local essential oils, and a rejuvenating facial. End with a private poolside dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with a selection of Vietnamese and Western options
meals.lunch: Farm-fresh lunch at Tra Que Village — simple, authentic Vietnamese village cuisine using organic produce
meals.dinner: Private in-room or poolside dinner at the resort — curated tasting menu with premium Vietnamese dishes and a bottle of selected wine

day_by_day.notes: My Son is best visited early morning to avoid heat and crowds — depart by 7:30 AM if possible. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring insect repellent for the jungle temple complex. The Tra Que Village experience is best booked through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Morning bicycle tour through Hoi An's tranquil countryside — cycle past rice paddies, water buffalo, lotus ponds, and traditional villages. Visit a local family home for tea and conversation. Collect your bespoke ao dai or tailored clothing order from Yaly Couture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Internal flight from Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) — approximately 1 hour. Private luxury transfer to your hotel in District 1 (Park Hyatt Saigon or Reverie Saigon recommended). Check in and freshen up. Afternoon exploration of the historic city center: Notre-Dame Cathedral, the Central Post Office (a stunning French colonial building), and Reunification Palace.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Saigon's legendary rooftop bar scene — cocktails at Chill Skybar (49th floor, AB Tower) or EON Heli Bar for spectacular panoramic city views as the sun sets over the Saigon skyline.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Hoi An before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Da Nang airport or upon arrival in Saigon — banh mi from a premium Saigon deli
meals.dinner: Dinner at Noir — Dining in the Dark, Saigon — a unique multi-sensory fine-dining experience served in complete darkness by visually impaired staff, featuring Vietnamese tasting menus

day_by_day.notes: Book the Da Nang to Ho Chi Minh City flight in advance. Reunification Palace has specific opening hours — check ahead. The Noir restaurant experience requires advance reservation and is one of Saigon's most unique dining experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure for a premium day trip to the Cu Chi Tunnels — the remarkable 250km underground network used by Viet Cong guerrillas during the Vietnam War. Book a private VIP tour with a specialist guide for an in-depth, crowd-free experience. Crawl through widened tunnel sections and learn about the extraordinary ingenuity and resilience of the Vietnamese people.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Saigon. Explore the vibrant Ben Thanh Market area and the surrounding streets for premium Vietnamese handicrafts, lacquerware, and silk. Visit the War Remnants Museum for a sobering and essential perspective on the Vietnam War's impact — one of the most important museums in Southeast Asia.
day_by_day.evening: Premium street food tour of Saigon with a celebrity chef guide — explore Districts 1, 3, and 4 on motorbike or by foot, tasting banh mi, hu tieu (Saigon noodle soup), banh xeo (sizzling crepes), and fresh sugarcane juice at authentic local stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — extensive buffet at the Park Hyatt or Reverie featuring live cooking stations, Vietnamese and international options
meals.lunch: Lunch near Cu Chi — traditional Southern Vietnamese countryside cuisine featuring clay pot dishes, fresh herbs, and river fish
meals.dinner: Street food tour dinner — multiple tastings across 6–8 premium street food stops in Saigon's most authentic neighborhoods

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable, dark-colored clothing for the Cu Chi Tunnels as crawling through tunnel sections can be dusty. The War Remnants Museum is emotionally impactful — allow adequate time and mental space. The evening street food tour by motorbike is a quintessential Saigon experience — book with XO Tours or Saigon Street Eats.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Vietnam — leisurely breakfast at the hotel. Last-minute luxury shopping in Dong Khoi Street (Saigon's most elegant boulevard) for premium Vietnamese silk, lacquerware, fine art, and designer ao dai. Visit the iconic Continental Hotel for a farewell ca phe sua da on its historic terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Premium half-day Mekong Delta excursion by private speedboat — glide through the lush waterways, visit a floating market, sample tropical fruits (dragon fruit, rambutan, jackfruit), and observe traditional cottage industries (rice paper making, coconut candy production). Return to Saigon in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Anan Saigon — Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's celebrated restaurant reinterpreting Vietnamese street food through a fine-dining lens, with a premium tasting menu and natural wine pairing. Transfer to Tan Son Nhat International Airport for departure.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the hotel — full Vietnamese and Western spread with fresh juices, pastries, and Vietnamese coffee
meals.lunch: Tropical fruit feast and local snacks during the Mekong Delta excursion
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu dinner at Anan Saigon — 8-course contemporary Vietnamese tasting menu with natural wine or cocktail pairing, celebrating the flavors of the entire journey

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your international departure for airport check-in and security. The Mekong Delta speedboat excursion should return no later than 4 PM to allow time for dinner and airport transfer. Request the hotel concierge to arrange a premium airport transfer. Keep one bag accessible for any last-minute purchases.
